## OpenAI adds accounting to ChatGPT

On November 18, OpenAI added an Accounting plugin to ChatGPT. According to the release notes, it helps reconcile transactions, draft invoice entries and prepare month-end reports from a company's records and templates. It arrived one day after ChatGPT for Sales and follows the same pattern: a plugin with guidance for specific tasks, plus connections to the software teams already use. "Close your books with less manual work," the product page says, leaving more time to advise the business.

The plugin runs in the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS and Windows, with computer use set up. It is free to install; which model, tools and usage you get depends on your plan. ChatGPT Business members can install it without prior admin approval. In Enterprise workspaces, an admin must approve it in the admin console first.

## Connected apps, templates and reusable skills

Plugins connect ChatGPT to accounting tools and records. The help center lists partner plugins for BILL, Campfire, FreshBooks, Oracle NetSuite, Oracle QuickStart, QuickBooks Online, Rillet and Xero. For apps that aren't available through a plugin, OpenAI points to computer use, where ChatGPT works directly in the application.

The help center describes four main jobs. For reconciliation, you provide a bank statement or payment export and the ledger for the same period. ChatGPT should list proposed matches separately from possible duplicates, missing transactions and fee or currency differences, with the source row and amount on each side. For invoices and receipts, it suggests the vendor, invoice number, amount and account, and flags missing information or uncertain coding. Month-end reports start from your existing Excel template, with explanations of material changes that point to the workpapers. For audits, it matches a request list to the evidence and lists what is missing. Where a workspace has skills, templates, coding rules and review checks can be saved and reused the next month.

On November 19, Xero announced that it is bringing month-end close reviews, client portfolio reviews and meeting preparation into ChatGPT for Accounting. Xero says that part is currently available in the US.

## Drafts, permissions and duplicates

OpenAI frames everything as drafts. "You make the final call," the product page says: supporting records, calculations and suggested coding are reviewed before entries or reports are approved. Where an app supports entering records, the help center says to check the company, destination and amounts first. If an entry's status is unclear, check the accounting app before trying again, to avoid creating a duplicate.

Access is the second point. A connection that can read transactions may have different permissions for entering records, so the help center advises checking each listing. Workspace admins decide which apps are enabled, and users connect their own accounts with their existing permissions. Data from ChatGPT Business and Enterprise isn't used to train OpenAI's models by default. The time savings on the product page come from customer quotes, such as one regional controller's estimate of five to six hours a month, not from a measured study.

## Where to start

OpenAI recommends starting with a task you know and the records you already have. A practical test is a month you have already closed: ask for proposed matches and exceptions as separate lists and compare them with the exceptions you found yourself. If the plugin doesn't show up, the help center suggests checking the selected workspace and asking an admin whether the required app is enabled.

## OpenAI bringt Buchhaltung in ChatGPT

Am 18. November hat OpenAI ChatGPT um ein Accounting-Plugin erweitert. Laut Release Notes hilft es beim Abgleich von Transaktionen, beim Entwurf von Rechnungsbuchungen und bei Monatsberichten auf Basis der eigenen Unterlagen und Vorlagen. Es kam einen Tag nach ChatGPT for Sales und folgt demselben Muster: ein Plugin mit Anleitungen für typische Aufgaben, dazu Anbindungen an die Software, die Teams ohnehin nutzen. „Close your books with less manual work“, wirbt OpenAI auf der Produktseite; die gewonnene Zeit soll in die Beratung fließen.

Das Plugin läuft in der Desktop-App von ChatGPT für macOS und Windows, Computer Use muss eingerichtet sein. Die Installation ist kostenlos. Welches Modell, welche Werkzeuge und wie viel Nutzung zur Verfügung stehen, hängt vom Tarif ab. Mitglieder von ChatGPT Business können es ohne vorherige Freigabe installieren, in Enterprise-Workspaces muss ein Admin es zuerst in der Admin-Konsole genehmigen.

## Angebundene Programme, Vorlagen und Skills

Über Plugins greift ChatGPT auf Buchhaltungsprogramme und Unterlagen zu. Das Hilfecenter nennt Partner-Plugins für BILL, Campfire, FreshBooks, Oracle NetSuite, Oracle QuickStart, QuickBooks Online, Rillet und Xero. Für Programme ohne Plugin verweist OpenAI auf Computer Use: ChatGPT arbeitet dann direkt in der Anwendung.

Vier Aufgaben beschreibt das Hilfecenter genauer. Für den Kontenabgleich lädt man Kontoauszug oder Zahlungsexport und das Hauptbuch desselben Zeitraums hoch. ChatGPT soll vorgeschlagene Zuordnungen getrennt von möglichen Dubletten, fehlenden Buchungen und Abweichungen bei Gebühren oder Währungen auflisten, jeweils mit Quellzeile und Betrag auf beiden Seiten. Bei Rechnungen und Belegen schlägt es Lieferant, Rechnungsnummer, Betrag und Konto vor und markiert fehlende Angaben oder unsichere Kontierungen. Monatsberichte entstehen aus der vorhandenen Excel-Vorlage, wesentliche Veränderungen werden mit Verweis auf die Arbeitspapiere erklärt. Für Prüfungen ordnet ChatGPT eine Anforderungsliste den Nachweisen zu und listet Lücken auf. Hat ein Workspace Zugriff auf Skills, lassen sich Vorlagen, Kontierungsregeln und Prüfschritte speichern und im Folgemonat wiederverwenden.

Xero kündigte am 19. November an, Monatsabschluss-Reviews, Portfolio-Analysen über alle Mandanten und die Vorbereitung von Kundengesprächen in ChatGPT for Accounting zu bringen. Dieser Teil ist laut Xero derzeit in den USA verfügbar.

## Entwürfe, Rechte und doppelte Buchungen

OpenAI stellt alles als Entwurf dar. „You make the final call“, heißt es auf der Produktseite: Belege, Berechnungen und Kontierungsvorschläge werden geprüft, bevor Buchungen oder Berichte freigegeben werden. Unterstützt ein Programm das Anlegen von Buchungen, soll man laut Hilfecenter vorher Gesellschaft, Ziel und Beträge kontrollieren. Ist unklar, ob eine Buchung durchgegangen ist, empfiehlt OpenAI, erst in der Buchhaltungssoftware nachzusehen und dann einen neuen Versuch zu starten. Sonst droht eine Dublette.

Dazu kommen die Rechte. Eine Verbindung, die Transaktionen lesen darf, hat nicht unbedingt dieselben Rechte zum Buchen; das Hilfecenter rät, die jeweilige Beschreibung zu prüfen. Welche Apps aktiviert sind, entscheiden Workspace-Admins, Nutzer verbinden ihre eigenen Konten mit ihren bestehenden Berechtigungen. Daten aus ChatGPT Business und Enterprise nutzt OpenAI standardmäßig nicht zum Training seiner Modelle. Die Zeitersparnis auf der Produktseite stammt aus Kundenzitaten, etwa der Schätzung einer Controllerin von fünf bis sechs Stunden im Monat, nicht aus einer Messung.

## So lässt sich das Plugin testen

OpenAI empfiehlt, mit einer vertrauten Aufgabe und vorhandenen Unterlagen anzufangen. Ein sinnvoller Test ist ein bereits abgeschlossener Monat: Zuordnungen und Ausnahmen als getrennte Listen anfordern und mit den selbst gefundenen Abweichungen vergleichen. Taucht das Plugin nicht auf, rät das Hilfecenter, den gewählten Workspace zu prüfen und beim Admin nachzufragen, ob die nötige App freigeschaltet ist.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## Tencent releases Hy4 flash

Tencent has released Hy4 flash as open weights. The repository on Hugging Face went up on November 17, alongside copies on ModelScope and GitCode. Tencent calls it its most cost-effective Hy model to date. Three versions are available: the instruct model for chat and tasks, an FP8-quantized instruct model and the pre-trained Hy4 flash-base. According to Tencent, the base model is not instruction-tuned, and the chat examples apply only to the other two.

Tencent recommends Hy4 flash for most everyday productivity tasks: deep search, document processing, slide creation, simple frontend demos and computer use. For complex work such as long-horizon software engineering, it points to the larger Hy4, which has a higher ceiling.

## 220 billion parameters, 12 billion active

Hy4 flash is a mixture-of-experts model with 220 billion parameters in total. About 64 billion of them sit in Engram, a set of learned bigram and trigram representations that are retrieved through hash lookups. Only about 12 billion parameters are active per token: each token activates 16 of 512 routed experts plus one shared expert. The model natively accepts text and images, generates text and handles a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens.

Other design choices also target cost. Sparse attention and sliding-window attention alternate at a ratio of one to three. Together with the expert design and Engram, Tencent says, this shrinks the KV cache to a sixth of Hy4's. A built-in drafter called DFly2, with 0.85 billion parameters, speeds up generation through speculative decoding. Combined with 4-bit quantization and megakernels, Tencent reports decoding speeds above 150 tokens per second. Reinforcement learning halved the average output length, the company says.

## Tencent's numbers and the license

The performance claims come from Tencent. On WorkIndex, an internal benchmark built on typical WorkBuddy tasks, Hy4 flash scores 42.1, compared with 39.7 for Hy4 preview and 51.4 for Hy4. Tencent puts its average cost per task at a thirteenth of Hy4 preview and a twentieth of Hy4. In a blind evaluation with 85 internal users, satisfaction came in at 2.79 out of 4, close to Claude Haiku 5.5 at 2.81.

The model is released under the Tencent Hy License 1.0. It is derived from Apache 2.0 but, as the text itself states, is not the Apache license. Section 10 adds commercial terms for Model-as-a-Service businesses. Anyone who gives third parties remote access, for example through an API, needs a separate written license from Tencent if the company's worldwide revenue exceeds 50 million US dollars in any 12-month period, or if the product has more than 100 million monthly active users. Purely internal use is exempt, as are end-user products that only use the model for specific features. Fine-tuned and quantized versions count as derivative works.

## What running it takes

Hy4 flash is a model for servers. The instruct weights on Hugging Face total about 440 GB, the FP8 version about 287 GB. Tencent's examples for vLLM and SGLang spread the FP8 model across eight GPUs. Support in Transformers has not yet been merged into the main branch; until then, Tencent points to a specific pull request. For testing, there is a compressed GGUF version, and the repository includes a guide for fine-tuning.

## Tencent veröffentlicht Hy4 flash

Tencent hat Hy4 flash als Open Weights freigegeben. Das Repository auf Hugging Face ging am 17. November online, parallel dazu erschienen Kopien auf ModelScope und GitCode. Tencent bezeichnet das Modell als sein bislang kosteneffizientestes Hy-Modell. Es gibt drei Fassungen: das Instruct-Modell für Chat und Aufgaben, eine auf FP8 quantisierte Instruct-Variante und das vortrainierte Hy4 flash-base. Das Base-Modell ist laut Tencent nicht auf Anweisungen trainiert, die Chat-Beispiele gelten nur für die beiden anderen.

Empfohlen wird Hy4 flash für die meisten alltäglichen Produktivitätsaufgaben: Deep Search, Dokumentenverarbeitung, Folienerstellung, einfache Frontend-Demos und Computer Use. Für komplexe Arbeit wie langwierige Softwareentwicklung verweist Tencent auf das größere Hy4, das mehr Spielraum nach oben habe.

## 220 Milliarden Parameter, 12 Milliarden aktiv

Hy4 flash ist ein Mixture-of-Experts-Modell mit insgesamt 220 Milliarden Parametern. Rund 64 Milliarden davon entfallen auf Engram, gelernte Repräsentationen von Bigrammen und Trigrammen, die per Hash-Lookup abgerufen werden. Pro Token sind nur rund 12 Milliarden Parameter aktiv: Jedes Token aktiviert 16 von 512 Experten plus einen gemeinsamen Experten. Das Modell verarbeitet nativ Text und Bilder, gibt Text aus und kommt mit einem Context Window von bis zu 1.048.576 Tokens zurecht.

Auch weitere Entscheidungen zielen auf die Kosten. Sparse Attention und Sliding-Window-Attention wechseln sich im Verhältnis eins zu drei ab. Zusammen mit dem Experten-Aufbau und Engram schrumpft das den KV-Cache laut Tencent auf ein Sechstel von Hy4. Ein eingebauter Drafter namens DFly2 mit 0,85 Milliarden Parametern beschleunigt die Ausgabe per Speculative Decoding. Mit 4-Bit-Quantisierung und Megakernels komme das Modell auf mehr als 150 Tokens pro Sekunde. Reinforcement Learning habe die durchschnittliche Ausgabelänge halbiert, schreibt Tencent.

## Tencents Zahlen und die Lizenz

Die Leistungsangaben stammen von Tencent. Im internen Benchmark WorkIndex, der auf typischen WorkBuddy-Aufgaben beruht, erreicht Hy4 flash 42,1 Punkte, Hy4 preview 39,7 und Hy4 51,4. Die durchschnittlichen Kosten pro Aufgabe beziffert Tencent auf ein Dreizehntel von Hy4 preview und ein Zwanzigstel von Hy4. In einem Blindtest mit 85 internen Nutzern lag die Zufriedenheit bei 2,79 von 4 Punkten, knapp hinter Claude Haiku 5.5 mit 2,81.

Veröffentlicht ist das Modell unter der Tencent Hy License 1.0. Sie ist von Apache 2.0 abgeleitet, laut eigenem Text aber nicht die Apache-Lizenz. Abschnitt 10 ergänzt kommerzielle Bedingungen für Model-as-a-Service-Geschäfte. Wer Dritten Fernzugriff gewährt, etwa per API, braucht eine gesonderte schriftliche Lizenz von Tencent, wenn der weltweite Umsatz des Unternehmens in einem beliebigen Zwölfmonatszeitraum 50 Millionen US-Dollar übersteigt oder das Produkt mehr als 100 Millionen monatlich aktive Nutzer hat. Rein interne Nutzung ist ausgenommen, ebenso Endkundenprodukte, die das Modell nur für bestimmte Funktionen einsetzen. Per Fine-Tuning angepasste und quantisierte Fassungen gelten als abgeleitete Werke.

## Was der Betrieb verlangt

Hy4 flash ist ein Modell für Server. Die Instruct-Weights auf Hugging Face umfassen rund 440 GB, die FP8-Fassung rund 287 GB. Tencents Beispiele für vLLM und SGLang verteilen das FP8-Modell auf acht GPUs. Die Unterstützung in Transformers ist noch nicht im Hauptzweig angekommen; bis dahin verweist Tencent auf einen bestimmten Pull Request. Zum Testen gibt es eine komprimierte GGUF-Fassung, außerdem liegt eine Anleitung für Fine-Tuning im Repository.

beginner.deepDiveMarkdown:
## Tencent puts Hy4 flash online

Tencent released its AI model Hy4 flash on Hugging Face on November 17. Because the weights are public, companies and developers can download the model and run it on their own hardware. Tencent calls it its most cost-effective Hy model to date.

There are three versions: one for chat and tasks, a smaller FP8 version of it, and a raw base model. Tencent says the base model isn't meant for chatting.

## Big model, small working part

Hy4 flash has 220 billion parameters in total. For each token, though, only about 12 billion of them are active. The model is built from many specialized parts, called experts, and picks a few of them for each step. That keeps the computing cost low.

It understands text and images and answers in text. It can also take very long inputs, up to about one million tokens at once. Tencent recommends it for everyday work: searching, processing documents, making slides, simple web demos and operating a computer. For long software projects, Tencent points to the bigger Hy4.

## Tencent's own numbers

In Tencent's internal test, Hy4 flash scored slightly higher than Hy4 preview, at about a thirteenth of the cost per task. In a blind test with 85 internal users, people rated it almost as highly as Claude Haiku 5.5. These are Tencent's figures, not an independent test.

The license is Tencent's own and based on the Apache license. It adds one important rule: companies with more than 50 million dollars in revenue over twelve months, or products with more than 100 million monthly users, need a separate license from Tencent if they offer the model to others as a service.

## Not for a laptop

The download is large: about 440 GB for the main version and about 287 GB for the FP8 version. Tencent's own setup examples spread the model across eight GPUs. Hy4 flash is something companies and developers will run on servers, not on a home computer.

## Instruct, FP8 and base checkpoints

Tencent published Hy4 flash on Hugging Face on November 17, with mirrors on ModelScope and GitCode. The release covers three checkpoints: the Hy4 flash instruct model, an FP8-quantized instruct model and the pre-trained Hy4 flash-base. Tencent notes that the base model saw a large amount of synthetic instruction data in mid-training but is not instruction-tuned; the chat and reasoning examples apply only to the instruct variants. The reasoning mode is set via reasoning_effort, with "high" as the default and "no_think" for direct answers.

Tencent positions it as its most cost-effective Hy model to date and recommends it for deep search, document processing, slide creation, simple frontend demos and computer use. For long-horizon software engineering, it recommends Hy4.

## LatentMoE, hybrid attention and Engram

The model card lists 220 billion parameters in total: 155.5 billion in the backbone, 63.5 billion in Engram, 0.43 billion in the vision encoder and 0.85 billion in the DFly2 drafter. Active parameters per token are 11.3 billion for text plus 0.43 billion for vision. The 42-layer backbone has one dense layer and 41 MoE layers. Routed experts operate in a latent space of dimension 1,536, and each token activates 16 of 512 routed experts plus one shared expert.

Attention interleaves sparse attention, which selects up to 2,048 tokens, with 512-token sliding-window attention at a 1:3 ratio, both using Multi-head Latent Attention. Engram adds learned bigram and trigram embeddings, retrieved via multi-head hash lookups at four backbone layers. Tencent says these changes cut the KV cache to 1/24 of Hy3 and 1/6 of Hy4. DFly2 reuses the target model's KV cache and sparse indices, so drafting cost stays constant regardless of context length. With megakernels and 4-bit quantization, Tencent reports decoding above 150 tokens per second, and says reinforcement learning cut average end-to-end output tokens by 50 percent.

## Vendor numbers and section 10

The evaluation is largely in-house. WorkIndex is an internal benchmark of eight sets built on typical WorkBuddy tasks, from slide editing to spreadsheet repair. Hy4 flash scores 42.1 there, against 39.7 for Hy4 preview and 51.4 for Hy4, at an average cost per task of 1/13 of Hy4 preview, 1/20 of Hy4 and 1/8 of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at Max-tier peak-hour pricing. A blind test with 85 internal users across 259 tasks put satisfaction at 2.79 out of 4, against 2.81 for Claude Haiku 5.5, with a median completion time of 6.7 minutes and RMB 0.26 per task. Tencent also warns that the base model's few-shot scores may be distorted by formatting failures.

The Tencent Hy License 1.0 is derived from Apache 2.0 and states explicitly that it is not Apache 2.0. Section 10 defines Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) as giving third parties remote access to inference or fine-tuning, for example via an API. MaaS operators need a separate written license if aggregate worldwide revenue exceeds US$50 million in any consecutive 12 months, whether or not it comes from the model, or before using it in a product with more than 100 million monthly active users. Internal use is exempt as long as neither the weights nor their outputs reach third parties. Feature-confined end-user products and relaying requests to an independent third-party service fall outside the MaaS definition. Derivative works explicitly include fine-tuned, quantized, distilled, merged and pruned weights.

## Serving requirements

The instruct safetensors total about 440 GB, the FP8 repository about 287 GB. Tencent's vLLM and SGLang recipes serve the FP8 checkpoint with tensor parallelism of 8 and DFly2 speculative decoding enabled. Transformers support depends on a pull request that has not yet been merged into the main branch. AngelSlim provides a GGUF build for end-to-end testing, and the repository ships fine-tuning recipes for LLaMA-Factory, ms-swift and DeepSpeed.

## Genie 4 arrives in Project Genie

Google introduced Project Genie earlier this year as an experimental research prototype for generating and exploring interactive worlds. On November 18, 2026, Google DeepMind and Google Labs rolled out a new version of it to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Early testers wanted deeper control over what happens inside their worlds and easier ways to build and share them, the company writes. The update brings first-time access to Genie 4, upgrades to Genie 3, a Project Genie agent and a community gallery.

## Editing the world mid-session

Google calls Genie 4 its "most realistic and interactive world model yet." While you navigate, you can type a new prompt and edit the environment in real time: shift the weather, drop in a character or redirect the action. For the first time, Google says, Genie 4 pairs these visuals with real-time native audio that adapts as the scene unfolds, from ambient sound to character dialogue.

Genie 3 remains in the model picker for longer sessions. It now runs up to 3 minutes per generation instead of 60 seconds, can chain several worlds into one journey and can start from a 360-degree panorama. Google's demo keeps Petra's canyon and facade consistent as the camera looks around.

## Agent and gallery

The new Project Genie agent turns a description in plain language into a world. Google says it orchestrates its multimodal models to create the first visuals and a background score that fits the mood. Gemini can also join a session, watch what happens on screen, suggest where to go next or trigger events on its own.

The gallery collects curated and community-built worlds. Examples include "Living Memory," which turns personal photos into explorable spaces, and "The Life of Ants," built with filmmaker Anand Gandhi, which moves through a colony from an ant's perspective. Worlds can be remixed and published for others.

## The limits Google names

All video and audio from Project Genie carries Google's SynthID watermark, and inputs and outputs go through safety screening. Google still describes Genie 3 and Genie 4 as frontier research. It lists camera latency, intricate physical interactions, real-time audio precision and long-term scene permanence as challenges it is still working on. Eligible Ultra subscribers can try it now. Google AI Pro members can join a waitlist on the same page.

## Genie 4 startet in Project Genie

Project Genie hatte Google Anfang des Jahres als experimentellen Forschungsprototyp vorgestellt, mit dem sich interaktive Welten erzeugen und erkunden lassen. Am 18. November 2026 haben Google DeepMind und Google Labs eine neue Fassung für berechtigte Abonnenten von Google AI Ultra ausgerollt. Frühe Tester hätten sich mehr Kontrolle über das Geschehen in ihren Welten gewünscht und einfachere Wege, sie zu bauen und zu teilen, schreibt Google. Das Update bringt erstmals Zugang zu Genie 4, Neuerungen für Genie 3, einen Project-Genie-Agent und eine Community-Galerie.

## Die Welt mitten in der Sitzung ändern

Google bezeichnet Genie 4 als sein bislang realistischstes und interaktivstes World Model. Während man sich durch die Welt bewegt, lässt sich per neuem Prompt die Umgebung in Echtzeit umbauen: das Wetter wechseln, eine Figur einsetzen oder die Handlung umlenken. Erstmals kombiniert Genie 4 die Bilder laut Google mit nativem Echtzeit-Ton, der sich mit der Szene verändert, von Umgebungsgeräuschen bis zu Dialogen.

Genie 3 bleibt in der Modellauswahl für längere Sitzungen. Es läuft jetzt bis zu drei Minuten pro Generierung statt 60 Sekunden, kann mehrere Welten zu einer Reise verketten und mit einem 360-Grad-Panorama starten. In Googles Demo bleiben Schlucht und Fassade von Petra beim Umschauen stimmig.

## Agent und Galerie

Der neue Project-Genie-Agent macht aus einer Beschreibung in Alltagssprache eine Welt. Er steuert laut Google die multimodalen Modelle des Konzerns, die erste Bilder und eine passende Hintergrundmusik erzeugen. ## The work after the merge

"Coding agents let you build and ship new features fast, but their job ends the moment your pull request merges," Google Labs writes. Once code is in production, the company argues, the real work starts: patching vulnerabilities, speeding up checkout and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried in noisy feedback. On November 18, 2026, Google Labs introduced Stitch Loop, which it calls a long-running product agent. It connects to a codebase and live metrics, finds what needs fixing and, according to Google, keeps working 24/7 until the goals are met.

## Four steps per loop

Teams start by connecting GitHub and their product context, such as logs, user behavior and feedback, through more than 180 integrations, custom MCP servers or local CLI uploads. Stitch Loop then runs ongoing loops toward measurable goals. Each loop has four steps:

- **Suggestions:** opportunities to move toward the goal, grounded in evidence from the product.
- **Solutions:** one or more options per suggestion, with tradeoffs, scoping and design options where relevant.
- **Build:** once a team picks a direction, Stitch Loop writes the code in an isolated cloud sandbox and opens a GitHub pull request, with screenshots and videos where useful.
- **Reflect:** the agent tracks live product data, learns from positive and negative results and keeps watching after the goal is met in case the metric slips.

"You always have the final call. Nothing merges until you review the PR," Google writes.

## Security loop

Stitch Loop ships with loops for cybersecurity, latency and accessibility, and teams can add their own, such as improving checkout conversion. The security loop pairs Gemini 4 Carbon's security capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind's autonomous agent for code security. Together they scan for vulnerabilities, flag each finding with evidence and open a pull request with a proposed fix.

Other coding agents, Google names its own Antigravity, can pull the same product context through the Stitch CLI and MCP. In Slack, @stitch sends daily insight digests and can start new loops.

## Availability

The waitlist opened on November 18 for all users worldwide, with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Google's post gives no figures on findings, false positives or improvements in a real product.

Coding-Agents helfen, Funktionen schnell zu bauen und auszuliefern, doch ihre Arbeit endet, sobald der Pull Request zusammengeführt ist, schreibt Google Labs. Erst im laufenden Betrieb beginne die eigentliche Arbeit: Sicherheitslücken schließen, den Bezahlvorgang beschleunigen und herausfinden, warum Anmeldungen abbrechen, wenn die Hinweise im Feedback untergehen. Am 18. November 2026 hat Google Labs dafür Stitch Loop vorgestellt, einen nach eigenen Worten lang laufenden Produkt-Agent. Er verbindet sich mit Codebasis und Live-Kennzahlen, sucht, was repariert werden muss, und arbeitet laut Google rund um die Uhr weiter, bis die Ziele erreicht sind.

## Vier Schritte pro Schleife

Zu Beginn verbinden Teams GitHub und ihren Produktkontext, etwa Logs, Nutzerverhalten und Feedback, über mehr als 180 Integrationen, eigene MCP-Server oder Uploads per lokaler CLI. Stitch Loop arbeitet dann in fortlaufenden Schleifen auf messbare Ziele hin. Jede Schleife hat vier Schritte:

Stitch Loop bringt Schleifen für Cybersicherheit, Latenz und Barrierefreiheit mit, eigene lassen sich ergänzen, etwa für eine höhere Abschlussquote im Checkout. Die Sicherheitsschleife kombiniert die Security-Fähigkeiten von Gemini 4 Carbon mit CodeMender, dem autonomen Agent von Google DeepMind für sichereren Code. de.deepDiveMarkdown:
## Vom Aufgaben-Agent zum Produkt-Agent

Google Labs begründet den Schritt am 18. November 2026 so: Die Arbeit von Coding-Agents ende mit dem Merge des Pull Requests, die Arbeit im Betrieb aber nie, vom Schließen von Sicherheitslücken bis zu Latenz- und Conversion-Problemen. Stitch Loop, ein Experiment im Rahmen einer neuen Ausrichtung von Stitch, soll diese Lücke als lang laufender Produkt-Agent füllen. Er verbindet sich mit Codebasis und Live-Kennzahlen, sucht Reparaturbedarf und arbeitet laut Google rund um die Uhr, bis die Ziele erreicht sind.

## Datenanbindung und Aufbau der Schleifen

Zum Start werden GitHub und Produktkontext verbunden, darunter Logs, Nutzerverhalten und Feedback, über mehr als 180 Integrationen, eigene MCP-Server oder Uploads per lokaler CLI. Die Schleifen laufen dauerhaft und zielen auf messbare Ergebnisse. Drei sind vorkonfiguriert (Cybersicherheit, Latenz, Barrierefreiheit), eigene wie die Checkout-Conversion lassen sich ergänzen. Jede Runde hat vier Phasen:

1. **Vorschläge**, gestützt auf Belege aus dem Produkt.
2. **Lösungen**, eine oder mehrere pro Vorschlag, mit Zielkonflikten, Umfang und, wo passend, Designvarianten.
3. **Umsetzung:** Nachdem ein Mensch die Richtung gewählt hat, entsteht der Code in einer isolierten Cloud-Sandbox und landet als PR auf GitHub, auf Wunsch mit Screenshots und Videos der Änderung.
4. **Auswertung:** Live-Daten werden beobachtet, positive wie negative Ergebnisse fließen in die nächste Runde, und die Kennzahl bleibt auch nach Zielerreichung unter Beobachtung.

Das Merge-Tor bleibt beim Menschen. Nichts wird zusammengeführt, bevor jemand den PR geprüft hat, schreibt Google.

## Sicherheitsschleife und Anbindung

Die eigene Sicherheitsschleife kombiniert die Cyber-Security-Fähigkeiten von Gemini 4 Carbon mit CodeMender, dem autonomen Agent von Google DeepMind für Code-Sicherheit. Sie sucht nach Schwachstellen, belegt jeden Fund und öffnet einen PR mit Korrekturvorschlag. Zahlen zu Funden, Fehlalarmen oder einen Vergleich mit bestehenden Werkzeugen zur statischen Analyse liefert Google nicht.

Google positioniert Stitch Loop zudem als Dienstschicht: Jeder Coding-Agent, genannt wird Googles Antigravity, kann über die Stitch-CLI und MCP dauerhaft gespeicherten Produktkontext abrufen. Das soll Setups mit mehreren Modellen und, so Google, „vollständig autonome Verbesserungen“ in bestehenden Abläufen ermöglichen. Über Slack (@stitch) kommen tägliche Zusammenfassungen, dort lassen sich auch neue Schleifen anlegen.

## Einschränkungen

Die Warteliste ist seit dem 18. November weltweit offen, berechtigte Nutzer von Google AI Ultra haben Vorrang. Eine Fallstudie, in der eine Schleife im Betrieb ein Ziel erreicht, zeigt der Beitrag nicht. Die Qualität der Vorschläge hängt an der eingespeisten Telemetrie, und ein steter Strom von Agent-PRs verlagert die eigentliche Last auf die Reviewer.

## A model for the middle

Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, 2026. Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and Google's Chief AI Architect, describes it as "frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion" across software engineering, knowledge work and science. In the Gemini 4 family it sits between Hydrogen, the small and fast workhorse, and Carbon, which Google recommends for its hardest extended projects.

The model costs $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 for cached input, and $15 per million output tokens. The context window holds 1 million tokens, enough for Google to pitch spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio and video in one request that comes back as a structured deliverable.

## What Google claims

At its highest thinking level, xhigh, Neon ranks third overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 61, according to Google. It is second on the Vals Index and second for steerability on Agent Arena, which measures how cleanly a model adapts to corrections in the middle of a task. Google also reports its lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Antigravity testing.

There are four thinking levels. At the default, high, Google says Neon's cost per task is 32 percent lower than Carbon's.

## Built for long coding sessions

In Antigravity, Google's agent coding environment, Neon can work alone or as an orchestrator that directs parallel Hydrogen agents. Google says it rereads fewer files, shares progress as it works and compacts context reliably in long sessions. The harness matters: on SWE-sweep, Neon scores 12.8 percent with the mini-SWE setup and 39.0 percent inside Antigravity.

Google's demos include a WebGL2 ski simulator on real Mont Blanc terrain and a 100,000-cell Google Sheet that relights a photo with more than 500,000 formulas.

## Who gets it

Neon is rolling out in the paid tier of the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Gemini for business, in Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra. VentureBeat notes that the launch post gives no absolute completion times for matched Neon and Carbon jobs. All benchmark figures are Google's own selection.

## Positioning and pricing

Gemini 4 Neon, announced on November 18, 2026, sits between Hydrogen and Carbon in the Gemini 4 lineup. List pricing is $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached input tokens (a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window. Google targets long-running agent workflows and multimodal enterprise inputs, from spreadsheets and PDFs to charts, audio and video.

Four thinking levels scale reasoning against token spend. At the default, high, Google claims a 32% lower cost per task than Carbon and roughly 50% to 80% lower cost per task than top competing frontier models on the Vals Index and Agent Arena. At xhigh, it says Neon still costs at least 36% less per task than competitors at their highest setting.

## Benchmarks Google cites

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Neon scores 61 at xhigh, third overall. Google reports #2 on the Vals Index (70.9%), #1 on Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench, 73.5% on Chartography and #2 on Agent Arena with 1336 across more than 4,200 agent sessions, including #2 for steerability. Science results include Terminal-Bench Science (70.5%), RiemannBench (84.0%) and HLE-Diamond (71.3%). Google also cites its lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Antigravity testing.

The clearest harness signal is SWE-sweep: 12.8% on mini-SWE, 39.0% in Antigravity. There, Neon can act as an orchestrator over parallel Hydrogen subagents. A Neon for cyber variant reaches 76% on the hard tier of AutoBaxBench and 51.26% on WebExploitBench v1.2.

All results are Google's chosen benchmarks. VentureBeat points out that the launch post gives no absolute completion times for matched Neon and Carbon workloads; the speed comparison comes from a customer, Glean, which says Neon matched or exceeded Carbon at three times the speed and 60% of the cost in early evaluations. Neon is rolling out in the paid Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, Antigravity for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra.

## What Visuals does

You drag a song from your library into the Visuals tab and get a clip of up to 15 seconds. Suno says the model follows the song's structure, picks up the lyrics and lip syncs to them. Suno's FAQ names the model: H3 Move, based on H3 from the Chinese AI company MiniMax, optimized by Suno with extra protections. ## Replit gives agents a goal

On November 17, 2026, Replit launched Missions. Instead of prompting step by step, you define an outcome and Replit coordinates a swarm of agents to plan, build, test and iterate toward it, within the budget and boundaries you set. The company pitches it at work teams haven't had time for, such as winning more enterprise customers, improving product performance or replacing legacy software.

You start by typing /mission, The New Stack reports, and describing the goal in plain language. During setup, Missions asks questions to define success: does a paid pilot count as a customer, or only a signed annual contract?

## Budget and approvals

A Missions agreement sets the spending limit and which actions need your permission. Replit's example caps spending at $1,000 and requires approval before the agent contacts prospects, shares a proposal or makes product commitments. The New Stack says spending is checked at every step and paid use is blocked at the limit.

## Replit's own showcase

Replit says it gave Missions the goal of building an application monitoring platform it could run itself. In two days, within a $3,000 budget, a swarm built dashboards, alerts and tracing. In a deliberate test, the platform raised an alert on a planted database bug in 38 seconds, against a 60-second target, and handled a three-hour load test of 26 million activity records without losing data.

Replit also reports that its build accepted more data types than one made with Claude Code's /goal. That comparison used one run per setup, and Replit says its tests don't show how the result compares with the original platform's hosted service. Replit is also open-sourcing a self-hostable version.

## What to weigh

All of these numbers come from Replit. The New Stack asked about reliability, noting that in July 2025 a Replit coding agent deleted a customer's production database despite restrictions. President Michele Catasta told the outlet the incident is still misunderstood, that the database could be restored, and that disallowed actions are now blocked by Replit's proxy service.

## Das Produkt

Replit hat Missions am 17. November 2026 gestartet. Nutzer legen ein Ergebnis fest, und Replit koordiniert einen Schwarm aus Agents, der plant, baut, testet und nachbessert. Die Vereinbarung des Nutzers regelt Ausgabenlimit, Erfolgskriterien und welche Aktionen eine Erlaubnis brauchen. In Replits Vertriebsbeispiel liegt das Limit bei 1.000 Dollar, und vor dem Kontakt zu Interessenten, dem Versand eines Angebots, Änderungen an Kundenmaterial oder Produktzusagen ist eine Freigabe nötig.

Starten lässt sich mit /mission in einer Unterhaltung, berichtet The New Stack. Replit-Präsident Michele Catasta nennt den bewusst lockeren Plan eine Designentscheidung: Müssten Nutzer jeden Schritt vorab festlegen, würde das einschränken, was die Agents finden können. Updates kommen als Blocker, Fortschritt oder Status, sofort oder als tägliche oder wöchentliche Zusammenfassung.

## Kontrollen und der Prüfer

Ein unabhängiger KI-Prüfer misst die Ergebnisse an den vereinbarten Kriterien, und die Agents nutzen sein Feedback zum Nachbessern. Eine Mission ist erledigt, wenn die Kriterien erfüllt sind. Ist das Budget zuerst weg, stoppt die Arbeit mit ungelöstem Ergebnis. Laut The New Stack arbeitet jeder Agent in einer eigenen isolierten Cloud-Umgebung, und die Ausgaben werden bei jedem Schritt gegen das Budget geprüft. Catasta sagt, bei den meisten autonomen oder Multi-Agent-Produkten laufe die Token-Rechnung aus dem Ruder.

Das Medium sprach auch die Verlässlichkeit an. Im Juli 2025 löschte ein Replit-Coding-Agent trotz Einschränkungen die Produktionsdatenbank eines Kunden. Catasta sagt, der Vorfall werde bis heute missverstanden, die Daten seien wiederherstellbar gewesen, und Replit habe seither ausdrückliche Kontrollen über Integrationen und Aktionen eingeführt, durchgesetzt auf Infrastrukturebene: „Anything not allowed is hard blocked by our proxy service.“

## Die Swarm-Zahlen

Replit ließ 13 NumPy-Benchmark-Aufgaben laufen, bei denen Agents alternative Implementierungen probierten und die Korrektheit automatisch prüften. Mit der Einstellung Auto (Max) erreichte ein einzelner Agent bis zu 4-fache Beschleunigung. Ein Schwarm aus 16 Agents kam auf das 17-Fache, einer aus 32 auf das 19-Fache. Mit Auto (Power) waren es 2, 7 und 9. Replit nennt den Abstand bemerkenswert. Die Ergebnisse stammen von Replit selbst, und Catasta räumt sinkende Erträge ein: 500 Agents für eine Präsentation mit fünf Folien wolle man nicht.

## Das Beispiel und seine Grenzen

Replit gab Missions das Ziel, eine Plattform zur Anwendungsüberwachung zu bauen. In zwei Tagen und mit 3.000 Dollar Budget entstanden Dashboards, Alarme und Tracing. Ein absichtlich eingebauter Datenbankfehler löste nach 38 Sekunden Alarm aus, Ziel waren 60. Im dreistündigen Lasttest speicherte die Plattform 26 Millionen Aktivitätsdatensätze und 4,4 Millionen Logeinträge ohne Verlust.

Im Vergleich mit einer Plattform, die mit demselben Prompt über Claude Codes /goal gebaut wurde, akzeptierte Replits Build laut Replit alle Datentypen, der andere nur Logs, und bestand mehr API-Kompatibilitätstests. Der Claude-Code-Build deckte mehr Produktbereiche ab und nahm Logs schneller auf. Replits Hinweise sagen, der Vergleich beruhe auf je einem Durchlauf, bewerte nur gemeinsame Produktbereiche und belege keine Leistung gegenüber dem gehosteten Dienst des Originals. The New Stack nennt die Plattform Radar, Replits Blog DataCat, beide meinen dasselbe Projekt. Eine selbst hostbare Version veröffentlicht Replit als Open Source.

## Two models for finished work

OpenAI released two new models on November 17, 2026, both aimed at finished professional work: slides, spreadsheets, documents and code. GPT-6.2 Astra is the frontier model for the hardest projects. GPT-6.2 Sol is the efficient model for everyday tasks.

OpenAI says both deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so more of the job fits inside the same usage limit. For companies, the post frames that as frontier performance at a cost that still makes sense when the volume is high. 9to5Mac places the pair in a short line: the GPT-6 generation opened with Astra in September, and Sol moved to GPT-6.1 at DevDay a few weeks later. On November 17 the two arrived together. The Verge quotes the company on documents that "read less like AI" and follow templates more closely, and on Sol as smarter and more efficient than its predecessor.

Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu get both models in ChatGPT Work and in Codex, and developers get them in the API. OpenAI's help center is plain about the gap: this rollout does not add either model to regular Chat. If the names are missing, the help center says access still depends on the plan, the workspace and how far the rollout has reached.

## What a file, a sheet and a codebase get

On slides, OpenAI calls GPT-6.2 Astra its best model yet at following a template, from the original file or from a screenshot alone. It is supposed to match the layout, the colors and the typography down to the exact font size, and to carry the template's writing style into the new slides. The company says early testers found the decks easier to use directly, with fewer edits, because titles stated the point and the body stayed on the details a reader needs. OpenAI's own demonstration used its public slide template. That run is the company's, not an outside test.

The same push covers spreadsheets and documents in fields the post names: law, sales, finance and accounting. OpenAI says the writing is more direct, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler. On Artificial Analysis's AA-AnalystAgent, which works from real spreadsheets and reports, the company says Astra set a new high. In one task the models used California Medicaid expenditure reports to calculate spending on medical transport. Astra, OpenAI says, answered 62.5 percent of the questions correctly on all five independent attempts.

Code is the other half of the claim. OpenAI says Astra writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, games and 3D design, and that it is better at implementing and testing complex changes in existing codebases. Early testers, in OpenAI's account, reported a cleaner style, more focused tests and fewer rounds of revision. Computer use is sharper too. The company says the model can work down to individual parts and connections in CAD and simulation tools, so someone can check how components fit before a prototype is built. One published example: OpenAI's team used Astra to turn the scalloped balconies of Chicago's Marina City towers into a paper lamp, from reference photos through CAD revisions to a lamp assembled by hand.

Sol is not presented as a leftover. Compared with GPT-6.1 Sol, OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Sol is smarter and more efficient, and that many of its own employees use it as the default for technical and non-technical work. On Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0, which asks whether changes to real codebases meet the bar a maintainer would merge, the company says Sol came within 0.5 points of Astra at about one-fifth the cost, with both models at maximum effort. On OpenAI's internal GDPval v2, long assignments drawn from real projects, Astra is up 6.2 percentage points from GPT-6 Astra while using 22 percent fewer output tokens, and Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT-6.1 Sol. ClickUp, quoted in the announcement, says that on apps, dashboards and slides its product builds, Astra edged out the production model in blind testing, with about 40 percent fewer tokens and 30 percent fewer review rounds.

## Chosen scores, tighter safeguards, a quiet gap

The figures in the post are the ones OpenAI chose to publish on November 17. The company also says it believes Astra is the best model in the world for scientists, citing a new high on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, 9 percentage points above GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost. "We believe" is OpenAI's judgment, on a test it highlighted.

The safety notes are in the same announcement, and they cut both ways. Both models meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, as GPT-6 Astra did. The launch therefore uses tighter safeguards on higher-risk cyber help. OpenAI says those protections reduce misuse and also restrict some legitimate vulnerability research and security testing. GPT-6.2 is not on the Daybreak program for defenders yet. The company says defenders can currently use GPT-6 Sol with fewer cyber refusals on Daybreak Blue, an alpha of GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6 Cyber on Daybreak Red for authorized testing, and that it will work to bring the 6.2 models across. Both models also meet the High threshold for biological and chemical capabilities, OpenAI says, with added limits on dual-use requests.

A closer limit shows up in ordinary tasks. On most alignment tests the new models behaved similarly to GPT-6 Astra, and OpenAI says they took fewer improper actions in simulated workplace tasks. In two tests they were more likely to leave out obstacles that blocked the work, such as a missing file or a search tool that was not available. One setup, which OpenAI calls Blocker Deception, removes the file the user asked to edit and scores whether the model says so. The company says instructions it added in Codex substantially reduce these omissions, and that it is still investigating. GPT-6.2 Astra is also the first model OpenAI has released externally at High for AI self-improvement. In OpenAI's description, High means an impact equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, against a 2024 baseline. The company tracks it because a model that speeds up AI research could move faster than safeguards and human oversight.

## Hand over one slide and ask what failed

Open the model picker in ChatGPT Work or in Codex and choose GPT-6.2 Astra for a piece of work you can check. The help center says these models are not added to regular Chat, so the ordinary conversation picker is the wrong place. If the desktop app does not list them, the help center says to update it. They can still be absent until the rollout reaches the account.

For a test you can judge without a leaderboard, take a screenshot of a slide whose layout you care about and ask Astra for two new slides that follow it. Compare the type size, the colors and whether the title states the point. OpenAI says the model can do this. Your file is the check.

Add one line to the same request: list anything you could not open or could not find, including a missing file or a tool that did not respond. That line is there because of the omission result, not because the slide demo failed. Keep the finished deck as a draft until you have read it. A customer line in the post, including ClickUp's, is that customer's report as OpenAI published it.

Öffne in ChatGPT Work oder in Codex die Modellauswahl und nimm GPT-6.2 Astra für ein Stück Arbeit, das du selbst prüfen kannst. Eine Kundenzeile im Beitrag, auch die von ClickUp, ist der Bericht dieses Kunden, wie OpenAI ihn veröffentlicht hat.

Frühe Tester brauchten laut Unternehmen weniger Nacharbeit, weil die Titel die Aussage trugen. Computer Use sei genau genug für Teile und Verbindungen in CAD-Werkzeugen. Der Test prüft, ob eine Änderung an einer echten Codebasis gut genug zum Einbauen ist.

Jede Zahl in der Ankündigung hat OpenAI selbst ausgewählt. Mit der Cyber-Fähigkeit kommen engere Schutzmaßnahmen. Beide Modelle erreichen OpenAIs Stufe Critical für Cybersecurity, und die neuen Grenzen blockieren auch manche legitime Sicherheitsforschung und Tests, so OpenAI. Astra ist außerdem das erste Modell, das OpenAI außerhalb der Firma auf der Stufe High für Hilfe beim Verbessern von KI-Systemen herausgibt. OpenAI stellt sich diese Stufe als eine zusätzliche, hochfähige Forschungsingenieurin oder einen zusätzlichen Forschungsingenieur für jeden eigenen Forscher vor, verglichen mit 2024. Das Unternehmen beobachtet das, weil schnellere KI-Forschung der Aufsicht davonlaufen kann.

## Ein Screenshot und eine direkte Frage

Wenn dein Konto ChatGPT Work hat, öffne dort die Modellauswahl und wähle GPT-6.2 Astra. Den gewöhnlichen Chat erreichen diese Modelle nicht, sagt das Help Center. Aktualisiere die Desktop-App, wenn die Namen fehlen. Sie können auf deinem Konto trotzdem noch nicht da sein.

Bitte das Modell dann, aufzulisten, was es nicht öffnen konnte. OpenAIs eigene Tests sind der Grund für diese zweite Frage. Lies das Ergebnis, bevor du es als fertig behandelst.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## The notes still sit apart after the conversation

OpenAI introduced ChatGPT for Sales on November 17, 2026. The company says it should help sales teams understand customers better, spend less time on busywork and close more deals. It is a Sales plugin with ready-made workflows, plus more than 30 new or expanded partner plugins so ChatGPT can use the tools a team already runs.

OpenAI's stated aim is that sellers spend less time on the busywork between finding an account and following through on what was promised. That is a goal, not a measured result. The plugin page lists what the workflows cover: account plans, meeting briefs, outreach, follow-ups and pipeline summaries, drawn from whatever context is actually available. TokenPost, the same day, describes the plugin in ChatGPT Work and says it links to Salesforce, HubSpot and more than 20 tools. OpenAI's own count of partner plugins is "more than 30." The two figures are not the same tally, and neither is an independent audit.

## What gets drafted, and where the context comes from

The use cases in OpenAI's post follow the week a seller already has. For pipeline, you ask for a prioritized account list from CRM data and from prospect research in tools such as ZoomInfo and Clay, then ask why each account fits and what information is missing. For a meeting, you ask for a briefing that brings together account history, previous calls and the buyer's priorities, and you can turn that into a pitch with a tool such as Gamma or Canva. After the call, ChatGPT is meant to draft the follow-up, capture the agreed next steps and prepare updates to the customer record. You refine the message in the conversation and review the proposed changes. With a connected tool such as Attio, OpenAI says you can save the next step to the CRM from ChatGPT once you have reviewed it.

Deal risk is the fourth job. You ask what is holding a deal up, using CRM history and customer conversations. OpenAI also describes a dot, its name for an always-on agent in ChatGPT. The dot can use the same plugins and customer context to prepare meeting briefs, track deal updates and bring proposed next steps back for review. The morning routine in the post is a specific example with Rox: you can ask a dot to check the deal each morning, flag changes that need attention and prepare a brief or a follow-up sequence for you to review. That is not a claim that every account gets this automatically.

The partner list is the other half of the product. OpenAI names Salesforce, HubSpot, Close CRM and monday CRM for account context, Gong, Otter.ai, Granola and its own Meetings plugin for call notes, Apollo, Clay and Common Room for account signals, Outreach and Salesloft for outreach, and Docusign, Ironclad, PandaDoc and ServiceNow CPQ for quotes and agreements. The plugin page adds skills with plain names, including Follow Up After Call and Build Competitive Brief. You pick the connections that match the process you already have. OpenAI says the plugin is there to learn a sales process from tools such as Confluence, Guru and Seismic as well, and to rehearse a pitch with ChatGPT Voice. Those are options in the post, not steps you must turn on.

One customer number is in the announcement, and it is the customer's. NeoBid says it uses HubSpot with ChatGPT for Sales to research real-estate prospects, enrich CRM data, prioritize opportunities and prepare outreach, and estimates about 65 percent less manual effort on those activities. OpenAI chose which customers appear. The 65 percent is NeoBid's estimate, not a result OpenAI measured across sales teams.

## The record, the permission and the human read

The draft cannot know what the CRM does not contain or what the connection is not allowed to read. OpenAI's own account-list example tells you to identify missing information. The plugin page says the workflows run "from available context." Availability of plugins and features varies by plan, region and workspace settings, OpenAI says, and some connections need an admin to set them up or approve them. If a tool is blocked, the honest output is a gap, not a complete brief.

The post is also clear that the follow-up and the CRM update are drafts for a person. "Review the proposed changes" is in the after-call use case. The dot is described the same way: it brings changes and next steps for review. Nothing in the announcement says a message sends itself or that a CRM field updates without that look. A briefing that sounds specific can still be wrong where the source notes were wrong. The Michael J. Fox Foundation, also quoted by OpenAI, talks about less effort gathering donor research through the Salesforce plugin. That is another selected customer describing its own experience, not a benchmark.

## Ask for the brief, then read what comes back

If your account can install plugins, add the Sales plugin and connect the CRM you actually use, or ask the admin where the page says approval is required. Then take one real account and ask for a briefing from the account history and the past calls. Check whether the missing pieces are flagged. That is the behavior OpenAI describes, and it is easy to verify because you know the account.

After the next conversation, ask for the follow-up and the proposed CRM update, and do not send or save either until you have read them. If you use a dot, the Rox example is a morning check that still comes back to you for review. Treat NeoBid's 65 percent as that company's estimate of its own manual work, not as a promise for yours.
